_about: What the nightly run tests. ONE primary variable per batch of 3 videos; every other test stays fixed at its `control` option. The Monday plan (PLAN.md) assigns the options per video, the weekly review (REVIEW.md) measures the batch and closes it. Times are Europe/Madrid; the audience is mostly US (NY = Madrid - 6 h, LA = Madrid - 9 h).

protocol.primary_metric: watch_pct = average watch time / video length, per network, averaged over the networks the video went to. Views depend too much on algorithm luck; they are reported, not decisive.

windows.note: Verdicts use the 7-day figures. The 48 h figures are only an early read for the notification.

protocol.baseline: median watch_pct of the last 5 videos with role `base` or `control`. The 7 reels published before 2026-11-04 count as base.

roles.control: uses the control option, to refresh the baseline
roles.base: tests nothing (special-date or themed reels, or a day with no test); counts for the baseline

protocol.success: the variant beats the baseline by more than 20% on watch_pct in at least 2 of the 3 videos of the batch
protocol.failure: the variant is worse than the baseline by more than 20% in at least 2 of the 3 videos
protocol.inconclusive: anything else. Not 'it does not work': repeat the batch once with 3 new videos; if still inconclusive, close it as 'no detectable difference' and keep the control.

outcomes.adopt: status decided, the variant becomes the new `control` for every video
outcomes.repeat: same test, a new batch id

protocol.side_experiment: none. `variants.tiktok_mode` is `api` for every reel since 2026-11-15 (closed: API posts get the same views as manual ones).

batch.hypothesis: Instagram's 3-second skip rate decides reach (10 videos, 29/10-13/11: skip 33-42% -> 1,270-2,500 views; skip 44-57% -> 140-340 views) and viewers watch about 25 s whatever the length (62 s: 41% watched; 79-86 s: 22-30%). A 45-58 s reel should hold a larger share of viewers and keep Instagram showing it. Hook style stays at the control (question) so length is the only variable. Measured on the 7-day Instagram figures of the 3 variant videos (2026-11-16, 2026-11-18, 2026-11-23): ig_views and ig_skip_rate_3s against the median of the last 5 base/control videos (see `measurement` and `success`).

measurement.note: watch_pct is reported next to the length but NOT decisive here: a shorter video has a higher watch % by construction. Decisive metrics are Instagram only (YouTube and TikTok retention are not available in Metricool), 7-day figures.
also_report: watch_pct and absolute average watch time in seconds
measurement.baseline: median ig_views and median ig_skip_rate_3s of the last 5 videos with role `base` or `control` (final figures). Reference before the test, 2026-11-15: skip 33-57%, views 139-2,518 (very noisy).

batch.success: in at least 2 of the 3 variant videos, ig_views is more than 20% above the baseline median AND ig_skip_rate_3s is lower than the baseline median
batch.failure: in at least 2 of the 3 variant videos, ig_views is more than 20% below the baseline median
batch.inconclusive: anything else: repeat once with a new batch id (B2b-length); if still inconclusive, keep `standard`.
batch.adopt: if it succeeds, `short` becomes the new control. Check then whether to go back above 1 minute: TikTok Creator Rewards only pays videos over 1 min and needs 10,000 followers and 100,000 views in 30 days.
batch.note: Batch full since the Monday plan of 2026-11-16: variants 2026-11-16, 2026-11-18 and 2026-11-23 (2026-11-21 is the themed Thanksgiving reel, role base, length standard). reads.note: Early reads only (provisional). Both published variants are >20% below the baseline median on IG views; if that holds at 7 days the batch closes as failure (2 of 3 below -20%). Absolute average watch time fell to 9.5-16.5 s (standard reels: ~21-27 s), so shorter reels are not keeping the same seconds watched. Closes once 2026-11-23 has 7-day figures (after 2026-11-30 20:30, so most likely the review of 2026-12-07).

queue.hypothesis: A surprising-statement hook holds more viewers than a direct question (repeat of the inconclusive B1, 3 new variant videos, same success rule on watch_pct).
queue.why: B1-hook-style closed inconclusive on 2026-11-23 (+23.7, -2.7, -5.4% vs baseline); the protocol repeats it once. Placed after time_slots because the owner moved time_slots to the front on 2026-11-15; swap if the owner prefers.
does a second signature touch help

history.hypothesis: A hook that opens with a surprising statement and then asks the question holds more viewers than a direct question, because it gives a reason to stay in the first 3 seconds. Measured on watch_pct (7-day figures, averaged over the networks with data; today Instagram only) of the 3 variant videos (2026-11-06, 2026-11-08, 2026-11-11) against the baseline (median watch_pct of the last 5 base/control videos). Success: the variant beats the baseline by >20% in at least 2 of the 3; failure: worse by >20% in at least 2 of the 3; anything else inconclusive (repeat once).

Neither success nor failure: inconclusive, not 'statement does not work'. Per protocol, repeat once as B1b-hook-style (queued); if B1b is also inconclusive, close as 'no detectable difference' and keep `question`.

options.00:30: 6:30 pm NY (3:30 pm LA), the US evening window; added 15/11/2026 because Instagram/TikTok engagement for US audiences peaks in the evening and 20:30 Madrid is 2:30 pm NY

time_slots.rule: fixed: always use `control`. testing: use the option the week plan assigns in `experiment`; if the plan has no entry for today, alternate (the option with fewer videos in the log). decided: `control` is the winner and stays fixed.
time_slots.note_2026_11_16: La usuaria decidió el 16/11 publicar el reel de ese día a las 00:30 (18:30 NY) sin esperar a cerrar B2-length. Es un dato adelantado del test de horario, NO una tanda: 2026-11-16 mezcla length=short y time_slot=00:30, así que no cuenta limpio para ninguno de los dos; mencionarlo al medir.

options.question: the hook is a direct question ('Why do cats purr?')
options.statement: a surprising statement, then the question ('Slaves didn't build the pyramids. So who did?')

hook_style.rule: fixed: always use `control`. testing: use the option the week plan assigns in `experiment`; if the plan has no entry for today, alternate (the option with fewer videos in the log). decided: `control` is the winner and stays fixed.
hook_style.note: 23/11/2026: B1-hook-style closed as inconclusive (see history). Not decided: `question` stays the control and B1b-hook-style is queued for one repeat. Until then, always use `question`.

options.teaser: hook + one line that teases the twist, without giving the answer
options.question_cta: hook + a question inviting comments ('Did you know this? 👇')

caption_style.rule: fixed: always use `control`. testing: use the option the week plan assigns in `experiment`; if the plan has no entry for today, alternate (the option with fewer videos in the log). decided: `control` is the winner and stays fixed.

personality.rule: fixed: always use `control`. testing: use the option the week plan assigns in `experiment`; if the plan has no entry for today, alternate (the option with fewer videos in the log). decided: `control` is the winner and stays fixed.

format.rule: Not an experiment: the formats vary on purpose so the channel does not look like a mass-produced series. Use the format with the fewest reels in the log (ties: the one used longest ago). Never the same format twice in a row. Themed (special-date) reels may use any format. The review records the format of every video and mentions it if it clearly explains a result.

options.standard: script 160-210 words, final video 63-75 s (QA warns above 85 s, refuses under 61 s). Profile `standard` in factory/brand.py
options.short: script 115-150 words, final video 45-58 s (QA warns above 62 s, refuses under 42 s). Profile `short`; run render, QA and the word gate with the environment variable REEL_LENGTH=short

length.rule: testing: use the option the week plan assigns in `experiment`; if the plan has no entry for today use the control. Shorter videos are NOT a way to skip the retention rules: the hook, the new-visual-every-3-4-seconds rule and the verification stay the same.

future_ideas.what: reels of 15-25 s with a single fact about the body or the brain and a personal claim in second 0 (as @the_psych_files does, 11-13 s, up to 19.7M views)
